cases.description: Pete offering language — 'Offering balance of IREN' is a limit sell order, not a confirmed exit

input.rawHtml: Offering balance of IREN at $49.40. I am expecting at least one more push higher and I will take gains into it.
input.author: Pete

cases.notes: LLM classified 'Offering balance' as CLOSE. 'Offering' means placing a limit sell order (not yet filled). Trader explicitly says 'I am expecting at least one more push higher' — forward-looking, not a confirmed exit. Real backtest hit: trade 70ac33f4 in bt:minimum-hippopotamus, premature close cost ~$6.50.

cases.description: Pete conditional language — 'I am trying to sell' is aspirational, not a confirmed exit

input.rawHtml: BE I am trying to sell for a $1 gain.
input.author: Pete

cases.notes: LLM classified 'trying to sell' as CLOSE. 'Trying to' is conditional/aspirational — the sell has not been confirmed. The real exit came 11 minutes later with an Exit badge (msg 465178). Real backtest hit: trade f6f0dacb in bt:minimum-hippopotamus, premature close orphaned the real exit.

cases.description: Pete offering half of a stock position — partial limit sell order, not a confirmed exit

input.rawHtml: Offering half of MSTR at $380. Want to lock in some gains on this move.
input.author: Pete

cases.notes: 'Offering half' means placing a limit sell on half the position. 'Want to lock in some gains' is aspirational intent. No badge, no confirmation of fill. Similar pattern to fp-exit-004 but with fractional quantity language that could trick TRIM detection.
